title: Bounded-below cohomology comparison
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a ring, and $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{ét}}$
the comparison morphism. For $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\Lambda)$ the unit of the
adjunction between
$\nu_X^*:D^+(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\Lambda)\to D^+(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ and
$R\nu_{X,*}$ is an isomorphism

$$
K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*K\quad\text{in }D^+(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\Lambda).
$$

Consequently $\nu_X^*:D^+(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\Lambda)\to D^+(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ is
fully faithful, and there is a canonical isomorphism in the derived category
of $\Lambda$-modules

$$
R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\nu_X^*K)\simeq R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{ét}},K).
$$

More generally, for a pro-étale affine $U=\varprojlim_iU_i$ with $U_i$
affine and étale over $X$,

$$
R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{proét}},(\nu_X^*K)|_U)\simeq
\varinjlim_iR\Gamma((U_i)_{\mathrm{ét}},K|_{U_i}).
$$

The colimit here is a filtered derived colimit, so its cohomology is the
filtered colimit of the cohomology groups.

Coefficients are discrete, and modules are left modules. Thus module sheaves mean sheaves of left $\Lambda$-modules, equivalently modules over the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], in a common larger universe in which the underlying site categories are small. The small sites and comparison geometric morphism are those of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with its set inverse image applied to addition and every scalar action for any ring $\Lambda$. Derived categories are the localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; $D^+$ means cohomology vanishes sufficiently far below [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. The right derived functors of comparison direct image and sections at the terminal object use [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. A pro-étale affine is as in [sk-def-pe-morphisms]; the presentation above is indexed by a nonempty small cofiltered category, and the colimit is over its opposite filtered category.

proof.text: Specialize the generic Grothendieck-abelian comparison to left modules over the arbitrary ring. The existing exactness and additivity instances apply, and isIso_comparisonAdjunction_unit makes the underived unit invertible on every sheaf. Apply Adjunction.isIso_derivedPlus_unit_app_of_rightAcyclic to this unit and rightAcyclic_comparisonUpperStar_obj_of_injective. This is the existing bounded-below injective-resolution proof, including the actual derived unit, not a replacement by an abstract isomorphism. NatTrans.isIso_iff_isIso_app makes the whole natural unit invertible.

Mathlib Adjunction.fullyFaithfulLOfIsIsoUnit gives the FullyFaithful structure on the actual derived inverse-image functor. Unfold boundedBelowComparisonGlobalSections: its factors are unitors, associators, the whiskered invertible derived unit, the bounded-below/unbounded right-derived compatibility, and comparisonLowerStarCompRightDerivedGlobalSectionsIso. Every factor is invertible. The last is the existing canonical Leray isomorphism: comparison direct image preserves K-injectives because its left adjoint is exact, and its composite with etale sections is pro-etale sections at the same terminal object.

For the affine assertion, take K to be DerivedCategory.Plus.Q applied to the given bounded-below complex I. Every transition between affine stages is affine by the existing scheme instances. Apply proEtaleAffineContinuity to I and the identity identification of Q(I) with K. Its second clause makes affineContinuityProEtaleMap invertible. The given bounded-below termwise-injective J is K-injective, so the derived evaluation unit at J is invertible.

Write p for the descent to the section complex of J, q for the descent to sections of the termwise comparison pullback of I, and E for evaluation at the cone point. The cocone equations and naturality of each component of j give p = q followed by E(j). Naturality of the derived evaluation unit gives Q(E(j)) followed by its unit at J equal to its unit at the pullback of I followed by RE(Q(j)). Expand affineContinuityProEtaleMap and cancel the exact-functor factorization isomorphisms. Hence Q(p) followed by the evaluation unit at J equals affineContinuityProEtaleMap followed by RE of the exact-functor factorization and Q(j). The right side is invertible since j is a quasi-isomorphism; cancellation proves the first affine clause.

Prove filteredHomologyPreserves directly from exact filtered colimits of left modules. Regard a diagram of short complexes as a short complex S of diagrams. Evaluation identifies S.homology with the diagram of homologies, naturally. Exactness of colim identifies colim(S.homology) with the homology of its image; homologyMap_mapNatTrans verifies the cocone legs. Thus short-complex homology preserves filtered colimits. Taking the three adjacent terms preserves colimits degreewise, so the same holds for complex homology in every degree. Since Q(p) is invertible, p is a quasi-isomorphism and H^n(p) is invertible. Transport the homology of the standard colimit cocone across this isomorphism. Functoriality and the descent equation identify its legs with the prescribed homology cocone, proving its colimit property.
